title: Transport a mate through conjugation and cancel an open factor
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal D,\mathcal E,\mathcal F$ be categories. Fix adjunctions $L_r:\mathcal D\rightleftarrows\mathcal A:R_r$, $L_p:\mathcal E\rightleftarrows\mathcal B:R_p$, $J_i:\mathcal D\rightleftarrows\mathcal E:P_i$, $J_b:\mathcal F\rightleftarrows\mathcal B:P_b$, and $L_q:\mathcal D\rightleftarrows\mathcal F:R_q$, with left adjoints written first. Assume the unit $u_b:1\to P_bJ_b$ is invertible. Let $J_s:\mathcal A\to\mathcal F$ and $J_k:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be functors and let $\beta:L_pJ_i\cong J_bL_q$, $d:J_bJ_s\cong J_k$. Use composite adjunctions [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], and let $c:P_iR_p\cong R_qP_b$ be the right-adjoint conjugate of $\beta^{-1}$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. Given $\alpha:L_pJ_i\to J_kL_r$, let $\gamma:J_iR_r\to R_pJ_k$ be its mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. For $M\in\mathcal A$, suppose $f:L_qR_rM\to J_sM$ satisfies
$$J_k(\varepsilon_{r,M})\circ\alpha_{R_rM}\circ\beta^{-1}_{R_rM}=d_M\circ J_b(f).$$
Put $z_M=u_{b,J_sM}^{-1}\circ P_b(d_M^{-1}):P_bJ_kM\to J_sM$. Then
$$R_q(z_M)\circ c_{J_kM}\circ\operatorname{adj}_{J_i\dashv P_i}(\gamma_M)=\operatorname{adj}_{L_q\dashv R_q}(f).$$
No geometric assumptions, derived categories or equality of different chosen adjunctions are required.

proof.text:
Put $X=R_rM$, $Y=J_kM$, and $a=J_k(\varepsilon_{r,M})\circ\alpha_X:L_pJ_iX\to Y$. Denote the composite adjunctions $L_pJ_i\dashv P_iR_p$ and $J_bL_q\dashv R_qP_b$ by $A_1,A_2$. By [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], $\gamma_M=\operatorname{adj}_{L_p\dashv R_p}(a)$. The composite Hom-bijection in [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] therefore gives
$$h:=\operatorname{adj}_{J_i\dashv P_i}(\gamma_M)=\operatorname{adj}_{A_1}(a):X\to P_iR_pY.$$

proof.text:
Regard $\alpha$ as a square with first adjunction $L_r\dashv R_r$, second adjunction $A_1$, and intervening functors $\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal D}$ and $J_k$. Its mate has component $h$ by step 1 and [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Apply clause 3(a) of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] with the new second adjunction $A_2$ and $\tau=\beta^{-1}:J_bL_q\to L_pJ_i$. The conjugate $\tau^c$ is exactly $c$ by [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate], with direction $P_iR_p\to R_qP_b$. The clause identifies the mate of $\alpha\circ\beta^{-1}$ with $(cJ_k)\circ\alpha^\flat$. Taking its component at $M$ and writing its counit transpose yields
$$c_Y\circ h=\operatorname{adj}_{A_2}(a\circ\beta_X^{-1}).$$

source.place: mateEquiv_conjugateEquiv_vcomp, lines 485-502; abstract categorical normalization of Stacks Tag 07A7 (remark-base-change)

proof.text:
Write $T=J_sM$ and $u_b$ for the unit of $J_b\dashv P_b$, and $\eta_q$ for that of $L_q\dashv R_q$. The assumed factorization says $a\circ\beta_X^{-1}=d_M\circ J_b(f)$. Substitute it in step 2, and expand the unit of $A_2$ using [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] and the Hom formula of [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection]. Functoriality gives
$$c_Y\circ h=R_q\bigl(P_b(d_M)\circ P_bJ_b(f)\circ u_{b,L_qX}\bigr)\circ\eta_{q,X}.$$
Here $f:L_qX\to T$, so the composite inside $R_q$ has type $L_qX\to P_bY$.

proof.text:
Compose the equation of step 3 with $R_q(z_M)$. By the definition $z_M=u_{b,T}^{-1}\circ P_b(d_M^{-1})$ and $d_M^{-1}\circ d_M=1$, its right side becomes
$$R_q\bigl(u_{b,T}^{-1}\circ P_bJ_b(f)\circ u_{b,L_qX}\bigr)\circ\eta_{q,X}.$$
Naturality of the unit, supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection], says $P_bJ_b(f)\circ u_{b,L_qX}=u_{b,T}\circ f$. Cancelling the invertible $u_{b,T}$ reduces the display to $R_q(f)\circ\eta_{q,X}=\operatorname{adj}_{L_q\dashv R_q}(f)$ by the same node's Hom formula. Since $h=\operatorname{adj}_{J_i\dashv P_i}(\gamma_M)$ and $Y=J_kM$, this is the claimed equation.
